clue.text: Now and then, notice attraction going up and down

parts.note: to notice is to see, in the present tense, the 'now' of the clue
then asks for notice in the past tense: saw

explanation.surface: Every so often you spot something appealing that rises and falls, like a fickle infatuation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now and then' reads as 'occasionally', but it asks for the verb 'notice' in two tenses: present SEE then past SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a playground ride on which children rise and fall in turn, an amusement of the fairground sort.

clue.text: Obstructions from pack and the rest of the rugby team

parts.note: a pack of cards is a set

parts.words: the rest of the rugby team
parts.note: a rugby union side is the pack of forwards and the backs

explanation.surface: Something about rugby forwards and the rest of the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack' tempts as the rugby forwards, but here it is a set, as of cards; the other half of the team are the backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Setbacks are reverses or hindrances that hold up progress.

clue.text: Paint two animals, taking seconds

indicators.note: taking means the pair of animals takes in the letter

parts.note: an emu and a lion

explanation.surface: An instruction to paint a pair of animals, having second helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is a water-based paint commonly used on walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Yen or pound?

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks which currency; neither money sense is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a yearning (noun) and to throb with dull pain (verb).

clue.text: Right away, Bolt races around hurdle

indicators.note: around here means the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: away signals that the letter for Right is taken out of races

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt, the sprinter, runs on the track around a hurdle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolt looks like the sprinter's name, but it is anagram fodder; 'Right' is the usual R that comes out of the second word before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurdle is a barrier or difficulty in one's way, which is exactly an obstacle.

clue.text: Item of fake news involved 'Liberace Deaf'

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: A false story claiming the pianist Liberace was deaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazen untruth told without shame is just the kind of thing fake news purveys.

clue.text: Elite leak spreads in Vogue

indicators.note: spreads in means the leak goes into the middle of the phrase for vogue

parts.note: the rage is the current vogue, fashion
a leak is slang for a pee

explanation.surface: An exclusive leak appears in the fashion magazine Vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leak' reads as a news leak; it is the slang for urination.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the body of nobles, the aristocratic upper class of Britain.

clue.text: Data filed online: 100, 0, 0, 1000, 5?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a zero looks like the letter O
a second zero, another O
K stands for a thousand
5-down's answer ends in the word LIE; this is that word without its first letter

explanation.surface: A string of numbers filed as data online.
explanation.walkthrough: '5?' points at 5-down, BAREFACED LIE: LIE without its first letter gives IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser cookie is a small file of information a website stores on a user's computer.

clue.text: Last couples from drunken summer orgy get up and go

indicators.note: Last couples from takes the final pair of letters from each of drunken, summer and orgy

explanation.surface: The final pairs leave a drunken summer orgy, standing up and departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up and go' looks like a command but is a noun phrase meaning vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is vigour or drive, the vitality also called energy.

clue.text: I've been hit in fight with epée, ultimately

definitions.text: I've been hit in fight with epée, ultimately

indicators.note: in places the cry of pain inside the two end letters
ultimately takes the final letter of each of the words fight and epée

parts.note: OUCH is what someone says on being hit

explanation.surface: A fencer concedes a touch in a bout with épées.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: OUCH goes between T and E, the last letters of 'fight' and 'epée'.
explanation.definitionFit: Touché is the French call a fencer makes to acknowledge an opponent has scored a valid hit on them.

clue.text: Regret nothing, following heart at last for this

indicators.note: following means the regret and nothing pieces come after the heart piece
at last picks out the final letter of the word heart

parts.note: to rue is to regret
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A romantic resolves to have no regrets, finally following their heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'this', pointing back at the whole clue: following your heart and regretting nothing describes true love.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner one follows one's heart towards without regret is a sweetheart, a genuine romantic attachment.

clue.text: Heavy smoker cooked Provençal soup, beginning to puff away

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are stirred into a new arrangement
away takes the letter out of the soup's letters

parts.note: taken as written, the cedilla ignored

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of puff

explanation.surface: Someone who smokes a lot makes a southern French soup and goes off for a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy smoker' suggests a chain-smoker; it is a volcano. P from 'puff' goes from PROVENCALSOUP before the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervolcano is a volcano capable of a colossal eruption, emitting vast amounts of smoke and ash.

clue.text: Is Isaac oddly withdrawn about mount which Abraham was up on?

definitions.text: mount which Abraham was up on

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the kept letters are read backwards
with the odd-placed letters withdrawn, only the even letters of Is Isaac are kept

parts.note: taken as written; its even letters are kept

explanation.surface: Asks whether Isaac strangely went quiet near Mount Moriah, where Abraham took him to be sacrificed.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the odd letters of ISISAAC leaves SSA; 'about' turns it round. In Genesis 22 Abraham saddled his donkey for the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham rode a donkey on the way to sacrifice Isaac; the beast's older name is the one wanted here.

clue.text: Basic Instinct's visceral nude scene finally wrapped by cast

parts.note: visceral means of the gut

indicators.note: wrapped by means the final letters sit inside the word for cast

parts.note: to cast is to fling, throw

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of nude and scene

explanation.surface: A comment on the notorious nude scene in the film Basic Instinct and its casting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basic Instinct' looks like the film title, but read plainly it is the definition. 'finally' gives EE, wrapped by FLING.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinctive reaction one cannot fully explain is an intuition, the sort of hunch felt in the stomach.

clue.text: Colleague of Quince hiding, after dropping Independent to support The Sun?

indicators.note: to support means, in a down clue, this piece sits below the next

parts.note: the Sun is a star

indicators.note: after dropping means the letter for Independent is let go from the word for hiding

parts.note: veiling is hiding, covering

explanation.surface: The setter Quince's colleague goes into hiding after leaving The Independent to back The Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Quince and Robin Starveling are fellow workmen in A Midsummer Night's Dream; the setter's pseudonym is the clue's joke. In a down entry, VELING under STAR supports it.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Starveling, the tailor, is one of Peter Quince's troupe of amateur actors in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Once Shrek Two is out, get it

indicators.note: is out suggests the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Once the second Shrek film has been released, go and buy it.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp the situation, understand what is going on, is an idiom with the same meaning as getting it.

clue.text: Sure fit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an assenting reply, all right

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that look like a pair of adjectives each define the answer on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase serves as a reply of agreement and also describes someone in excellent health.

clue.text: Discs for smutty flicks that contain a lot of butts

definitions.text: Discs for smutty flicks that contain a lot of butts

parts.words: Discs for smutty flicks that contain a lot of butts
parts.note: read as DVDs of pornographic films full of bottoms, but the flicks are flicks of ash and the butts are cigarette ends

explanation.walkthrough: Smut is soot, flicks are taps of a cigarette, and butts are stubs, so the dishes are receptacles for a smoker.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokers' round dishes collect flicked cinders and discarded cigarette stubs.

clue.text: Finally quitting Taskmaster, Greg Davies played parts in Hamlet

indicators.note: Finally takes the last letter of each of quitting and Taskmaster
played suggests the letters are performed in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Greg Davies, the comedian who hosts the TV game show Taskmaster, leaves it to act in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: G and R, the last letters of 'quitting' and 'Taskmaster', join GREGDAVIES for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The two clowns who dig Ophelia's grave in Act 5 of Shakespeare's play are roles called gravediggers.

clue.text: American network with broadband speed charges that are devastating

parts.note: HBO is a US television network
Mbps, often written MB/s, is a broadband speed in megabits per second

explanation.surface: An American TV network with fast broadband has fees that are ruinous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' looks like fees but means explosive devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen bombs are thermonuclear weapons of enormous destructive power.

clue.text: Bond reported, after his boss discovered raid for cocktail

indicators.note: after means the bond piece follows the others

parts.note: M is James Bond's boss in MI6

indicators.note: discovered strips off the outer letters, the cover, of raid
reported means the word for bond is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: James Bond, having reported back after his boss found out about a raid, wants a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the head of MI6 in the Bond books and films; 'discovered' means uncovered, the outer letters stripped off.
explanation.definitionFit: A mai tai is a rum-based Tiki drink with lime and orgeat.

clue.text: Clue for 'baker' slowing down solution?

parts.note: read as an anagram clue, the word brake made fluid (rearranged) gives baker

explanation.surface: A question about how to clue the word baker.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BRAKE (fodder) plus FLUID (an anagram signal) and it is itself a clue to 'baker'. Brake fluid is the hydraulic liquid in a car's braking system.
explanation.definitionFit: The hydraulic liquid that transmits pedal pressure to a car's brakes is a liquid for bringing the vehicle to a halt.

clue.text: On both sides of the Pyrenees, joiners are all the same

parts.words: On both sides of the Pyrenees
parts.note: south of the Pyrenees, in Spanish, the joining word 'and' is Y
north of the Pyrenees, in French, the joining word 'and' is ET

explanation.surface: Carpenters in France and Spain are just alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiners' looks like carpenters but means conjunctions: Spanish Y then French ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet works as an adverb meaning nevertheless, despite that, which is what 'all the same' says.

clue.text: Perhaps Trump curtailed old defence system

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, the last letter, is cut from the name

parts.note: Judd Trump is an English snooker champion; Perhaps flags him as one example of a Trump

explanation.surface: Suggests Donald Trump scrapped an old missile defence system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' calls up Donald, but it is Judd Trump, the snooker player.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo is a Japanese martial art of unarmed self-protection using throws and holds.

clue.text: This writer's just topped Absolutely Fabulous

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves: my

indicators.note: topped means the head is cut off, removing the opening letter of the word for just

parts.note: just means morally right, ethical

explanation.surface: The setter declares they have just beaten the sitcom Absolutely Fabulous.
explanation.walkthrough: MY plus ETHICAL with its first letter removed, THICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its literal sense means belonging to fable, legendary rather than real.

clue.text: Cry in the bath about cake Prue initially discarded

indicators.note: about here means the remaining letters are moved around into a new order
initially discarded drops the first letter of each of cake and Prue

parts.note: taken as written, before the first letters go

explanation.surface: Prue Leith, a judge on The Great British Bake Off, rejects a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: AKE and RUE are left once the first letters go; 'about' rearranges them. Archimedes is said to have shouted the answer in his bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes supposedly shouted this Greek exclamation of discovery when he stepped into his bath and saw the water rise.

clue.text: A little lad traps fly

indicators.note: traps means the word for lad holds the insect inside it

parts.note: a lad is a son
a midge is a small fly

explanation.surface: A small boy catches a fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a tiny amount, a variant spelling of smidgen.

clue.text: Piles can put off kisses and cuddles

indicators.note: put off means the word can is taken off the front of the longer word

parts.note: to canoodle is to kiss and cuddle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical complaint that can spoil romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piles' looks like the ailment, but it means heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for great quantities, heaps or lots of something.
